title: AI provider invocation metadata
description: What one call to an AI provider cost. Written once per attempt, including attempts that returned nothing, because a call that timed out still spent the budget and a ledger that only records successes understates the run. Sizes are measured bytes and are always exact; token counts appear only when a provider reported them.

id.description: Identifies the attempt this record is about, so records left by repeated legs of a relay can be told apart rather than summed twice.

attempt.description: Which schema-retry attempt this was. Attempt two and beyond is the cost of a rejected answer, and separating it is how a run shows what correction is worth.

status.description: answered: the provider returned text, whatever that text later proved to be. timed_out: the attempt was stopped without an answer. faltered: the provider failed in a way that says nothing about the request. failed: the provider failed in a way that will not come right on its own, so the run stops here — the call still happened and still cost what it cost.

purpose.description: What the call was for. artifact: the agent's own answer, whether a first attempt or a retry after a rejection. field_repair: a follow-up asking for prose that overran a schema limit to be shortened, which is a second call against the same attempt and would otherwise be invisible in the ledger.

usage.description: Null when no provider reported token counts. It is left null rather than filled with an estimate, because a guess written into the same field as a measurement stops being distinguishable from one.

source.description: Where the counts came from. Only a provider can measure them.

payload.description: A measured size. Bytes are what was actually written or received; characters are reported alongside because a multi-byte prompt costs more bytes than it does text.

sections.description: How a request divides up, so a prompt that grew can be attributed to the part that grew rather than to the call as a whole.
